translationRepairs: In the eighth year Cai Qian slipped into Dinghai to offer incense at Mount Putuo; Changgeng surprised him, and Qian escaped only with his life. Changgeng pursued him into Fujian waters until the pirate fleet was out of provisions and its sails in tatters. Qian then feigned surrender to Governor Yude, who sent Circuit Intendant Qing Lai of Xing-Quan-Yong to Sansha to negotiate. Yude abruptly ordered the Zhejiang fleet back to harbor, and Qian used the respite to refit his ships and escape.

In the eighth year Cai Qian slipped into Dinghai to offer incense at Mount Putuo; Changgeng surprised him, and Qian escaped only with his life. Changgeng pursued him into Fujian waters until the pirate fleet was out of provisions and its sails in tatters. Qian then feigned surrender to Governor-General Yude, who sent Circuit Intendant Qing Lai of Xing-Quan-Yong to Sansha to negotiate. Yude abruptly ordered the Zhejiang fleet back to harbor, and Qian used the respite to refit his ships and escape.
The source calls Yude a 總督, distinct from a 巡撫. The proposal fixes the rank, but the established title styling in this chapter is Governor-General, with both elements capitalized before a name.

In the summer of the ninth year, Lian Zong led more than eighty vessels into Fujian and killed Regional Commander Hu Zhensheng. An edict called for punishment of Fujian officers who had failed to reinforce, and Changgeng was placed in overall command of the naval forces of both provinces.

In the summer of the ninth year, Cai Qian and Zhu Fen entered Fujian with a combined fleet of more than eighty vessels and killed Regional Commander Hu Zhensheng. An edict called for punishment of Fujian officers who had failed to reinforce, and Changgeng was placed in overall command of the naval forces of both provinces.

Lian Zong is spurious: an external witness preserves the rare fleet character 䑸 where the local text has been flattened to 宗. The preceding sentence says Cai Qian joined Zhu Fen, so the subject is their combined fleet, not Qian alone.

In the summer of the ninth year Lian Zong led more than eighty vessels into Fujian and killed Regional Commander Hu Zhensheng; an edict ordered punishment for Fujian officers who failed to reinforce; Changgeng took overall command of the naval forces of the two provinces.

In the summer of the ninth year Cai Qian and Zhu Fen brought a combined fleet of more than eighty vessels into Fujian and killed Regional Commander Hu Zhensheng; an edict ordered punishment for Fujian officers who failed to reinforce; Changgeng took overall command of the naval forces of the two provinces.

The proposal correctly removes a nonexistent person but wrongly treats Qian as sole subject. The rare character 䑸 means a fleet, and the preceding context establishes the joined forces of Cai Qian and Zhu Fen.
In the eleventh year he died, and his grandson Jingbao inherited the title.
In the eleventh year of Xianfeng he died, and his grandson Jingbao inherited the title.

The preceding date frame is explicitly the Xianfeng reign, and the idiomatic field already identifies year eleven accordingly. Restoring Xianfeng in the literal field prevents a floating, ambiguous year.
He received generous posthumous care, was given the posthumous name Wuzhuang, and was granted the hereditary offices of Cavalry Commandant and Cloud Cavalry Captain combined.
He received generous posthumous care, was given the posthumous name Wuzhuang, and his family was granted the combined hereditary ranks of Cavalry Commandant and Cloud Cavalry Captain.

予...世職 is a hereditary award to the recipient's line, not an appointment held by the deceased. The proposal fixes the beneficiary, but ranks is more accurate than offices and matches the polished idiomatic field.
Delu served ten years as Fujian naval commander-in-chief, repeatedly memorializing on coastal defense and revising naval ship regulations, all of which were adopted.
Delu served ten years as Fujian naval commander-in-chief, repeatedly memorializing on measures for pursuing and capturing pirates and revising naval ship regulations, all of which were adopted.
緝捕事宜 concerns measures for pursuit and capture, not the broader subject of coastal defense. Naming pirates makes the contextual object clear and produces natural English without enlarging the claim.
The next day they tried again to intercept and encircle him. Qian fought as he fled, and by noon the pursuit had crossed the Black Water Sea into the deep ocean.
The next day they tried again to intercept and encircle him. Qian fought as he fled, and by noon the pursuit had crossed the Black Water Sea and reached green water.

見綠水 reports reaching or sighting green water after crossing the Black Water Sea; deep ocean is an unsupported interpretation. Reached green water is faithful and less awkward than the proposal's seen green water.

Following Lianggong in pursuit of Cai Qian, Buyun with forty men drove his boat straight against Qian's flagship in fierce combat; his vessel was small and no match; seeing the two commanders-in-chief arrive, he quickly threw fire pots to burn the bandit ship, hooked the rail with a long halberd, led several soldiers in leaping aboard, fought hand to hand at close quarters, and destroyed Qian's wife and her followers.

Following Lianggong in pursuit of Cai Qian, Buyun with forty men drove his boat straight against Qian's flagship in fierce combat; his vessel was small and no match; seeing the two commanders-in-chief arrive, he quickly threw fire pots to burn the bandit ship, hooked the rail with a long halberd, led several soldiers in leaping aboard, fought hand to hand at close quarters, and killed Qian's wife and her followers.
The object of 殲 is Cai Qian's wife and her followers, so killed is the idiomatic English verb. The proposal changes only that mistranslated verb and agrees with the existing event and death claims.
An edict praised Songnian's valor in destroying the ringleader, granted him the peacock feather, and gave him the hereditary office of Cloud Cavalry Captain.
An edict praised Songnian's valor in destroying the ringleader, granted him the peacock feather, and granted his family the hereditary rank of Cloud Cavalry Captain.

雲騎尉世職 is a hereditary rank transmitted through the family, not a personal office. The proposal fixes rank but still leaves the beneficiary ambiguous; the idiomatic field correctly makes the family explicit.
A military licentiate, he served in the navy under Li Changgeng, accumulated merit in repeated campaigns, and rose to brigade colonel on the provincial commander's staff.
A military licentiate, he served in the navy under Li Changgeng, accumulated merit, and rose to brigade colonel on the provincial commander's staff.

積功 states that Xu Songnian accumulated merit but does not itself specify repeated campaigns. Removing that unsupported embellishment leaves clear, grammatical English and preserves the career progression.
defeated Zhu Fen and Wushi Er at Gongzai Sea, and under Li Changgeng pursued and routed them at Jiazi Sea on the Fujian-Guangdong border.
again attacked Zhu Fen and Wushi Er at Gongzai Sea, and under Li Changgeng pursued and routed them at Jiazi Sea on the Fujian-Guangdong border.
又擊 means attacked again, whereas the following 追敗之 expressly supplies the later defeat. The proposal preserves that distinction and the lower-case continuation required after the preceding semicolon.
When Guoliang died he acted as regional commander of the Left Wing Town.
When Guoliang died he acted as regional commander of the Left Wing Garrison.
左翼鎮 is a named Qing military garrison command, not an ordinary town. Garrison correctly conveys the institutional sense and agrees with the already accurate idiomatic rendering.
Posthumous care was granted and he was given the hereditary office of Cloud Cavalry Captain.
Posthumous care was granted, and his family was awarded the hereditary rank of Cloud Cavalry Captain.
Because Xu Tinggui had just died, 予雲騎尉世職 grants a hereditary rank to his line rather than an office to him personally. Rank is also more accurate than office for 雲騎尉世職.
Gain and loss form a forest of examples—therefore there is no luck in it!
Here is a compendium of success and failure; there is no room for chance!

得失之林 describes a collected body of lessons or examples in success and failure. The proposal's record is defensible but less literal; compendium preserves the metaphor's function without the opaque forest calque.
